source: closed form. The curve is a flat 4.00 % continuously compounded SOFR discount curve, df(t) = exp(-0.04·t) on the ACT/360 axis from 2026-12-22; the eight knots are that function evaluated at t = 1/360, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and printed to full double precision, and log_linear_df reproduces a flat forward exactly between and beyond them. The schedule is WORKPLAN L507's: T+2 SIFMA spot (2026-12-22 + 2 business days = 2026-12-24), five annual anniversaries rolled modified following on SIFMA — 2027-12-24 is Christmas Day observed (a full SIFMA closure) so period 1 pays 2027-12-27, and 2028-12-24 is a Sunday whose Monday is Christmas Day so period 2 pays 2028-12-26. The expected values are the textbook single-curve OIS identities evaluated on that flat curve, not engine output: annuity = Σ τᵢ·e^(-0.04·tᵢ), float leg = N·(e^(-0.04·t_start) − e^(-0.04·t_maturity)) (the telescoped daily-compounding product, which the engine instead evaluates day by day), fixed leg = N·R·annuity, pv = float − fixed for a payer, parRate = float/(N·annuity), dv01 = N·annuity·1bp, curveDv01 = 1bp·N·(−t_s·df(t_s) + t_m·df(t_m) + R·Σ τᵢ·tᵢ·df(tᵢ)) — the analytic derivative of the payer PV under df(t) → df(t)·e^(−s·t). Currency tolerances are 1e-4 (a hundredth of a cent on a $100 mm ticket) because the engine accumulates ~1,300 daily compounding factors where this derivation telescopes them, which costs a few units in the fifteenth significant digit; annuity and parRate are pinned at 1e-12 and the per-period compounded rates at 1e-14.

closed form on a synthetic upward-sloping SOFR discount curve. The nine knots are round literal discount factors (0.98957 at 3M through 0.66914 at 10Y, an inverted-to-rising money-market shape) and the curve rule is log_linear_df, so ln df is linear between knots with the (0, 1) left anchor — evaluated here by a separately written two-line interpolator rather than by the engine's. The schedule is T+2 SIFMA spot from 2026-09-15 (= 2026-09-17), three annual rolls modified following: 2028-09-17 is a Sunday and rolls forward to 2028-09-18 without leaving September, giving a 367-day second period. The expected values are the same closed-form OIS identities as swap.ois.5y.flat, negated where the ticket is a receiver (receive fixed, pay float): pv = −(float − fixed), curveDv01 = −1bp·N·(−t_s·df(t_s) + t_m·df(t_m) + R·Σ τᵢ·tᵢ·df(tᵢ)). Tolerances as in that case, and for the same reason.
